pharm: Oral receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (VEGFR1-3, FGFR1-4, PDGFRalpha, RET, KIT)
quick: DTC: 24 mg once daily. HCC: 12 mg/day if >=60 kg, 8 mg/day if <60 kg. With pembrolizumab (EC/RCC): 20 mg once daily. With everolimus (RCC): 18 mg + everolimus 5 mg once daily
May take with or without food, at the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; effective contraception required during and >=30 days after
Do not breastfeed during and for >=1 week after the last dose
No adjustment mild-moderate; reduce to 14 mg/day (DTC/RCC-everolimus) or 8 mg (HCC) in severe impairment
Severe (Child-Pugh C): reduce starting dose; HCC not studied in Child-Pugh B/C
No specific interaction; avoid if hepatotoxicity
Blood pressure, ECG/QTc, LFTs, renal function, proteinuria (urine protein), TSH, electrolytes (Ca/K/Mg)
summary: Lenvatinib is an oral multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor with potent antiangiogenic activity, used for radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, and (with pembrolizumab or everolimus) renal cell carcinoma and endometrial carcinoma. It has numerous warnings - notably hypertension, cardiac dysfunction, arterial thromboembolism, hepatotoxicity, renal failure, proteinuria, GI perforation/fistula, QT prolongation, hypocalcemia, and impaired wound healing.
indications: Locally recurrent or metastatic, progressive, radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC)
Advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in combination with pembrolizumab (first line) or everolimus (after prior antiangiogenic therapy)
Advanced endometrial carcinoma (with pembrolizumab) that is not MSI-H/dMMR after prior systemic therapy

dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Manage toxicity by interruption/dose reduction (20 mg, then 14, then 10 mg)

dosage.d: 12 mg/day if >=60 kg; 8 mg/day if <60 kg

dosage.t: With pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks

admin: Take once daily at the same time each day, with or without food
If unable to swallow, may disperse tablets in water or apple juice
Withhold and reduce dose per label tables for adverse reactions
Control blood pressure before starting; withhold >=1 week before elective surgery (wound healing)
moa: Lenvatinib inhibits the kinase activities of VEGF receptors VEGFR1 (FLT1), VEGFR2 (KDR), and VEGFR3 (FLT4), and other pro-angiogenic and oncogenic kinases including FGFR1-4, PDGFRalpha, KIT, and RET, thereby inhibiting tumor angiogenesis and growth.

absolute: None per FDA label (no contraindications listed)
relative: Significant cardiac dysfunction / recent arterial thromboembolic event
Active bleeding / GI perforation or fistula risk
Severe hepatic impairment (HCC: avoid in Child-Pugh B/C)
monitor: Hepatic and renal function, urine protein

preg: Based on animal studies and mechanism of action, lenvatinib can cause fetal harm. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 30 days after the last dose.
lact: Because of potential serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose.
renal: No adjustment for mild-to-moderate impairment. In severe renal impairment, reduce the starting dose (e.g., to 14 mg/day for DTC and RCC-everolimus; 10 mg with pembrolizumab; 8 mg for HCC). Renal failure/impairment is a labeled risk - monitor and manage dehydration.
hepatic: No adjustment for mild-to-moderate impairment in non-HCC indications; reduce starting dose in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment. For HCC, use is based on Child-Pugh A; not established in Child-Pugh B/C. Hepatotoxicity (including hepatic failure) is a labeled risk.

major: Other QT-prolonging drugs (additive QT prolongation/Torsades risk)
minor: No clinically significant CYP-based interactions requiring dose change per label
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; minimize if hepatic toxicity present
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor BP, ECG/QTc, LFTs, serum creatinine, urine protein, TSH, serum calcium/potassium/magnesium

monitoring: Blood pressure (control before start, monitor weekly first 2 months then monthly)
Liver function tests (every 2 weeks for first 2 months, then monthly)
Signs of bleeding, cardiac dysfunction, GI perforation/fistula
counsel: Take once daily at the same time; do not make up missed doses if >12 h late
Monitor your blood pressure at home and report high readings
Report chest pain, severe headache, vision changes, black/bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, or unusual bleeding
Tell your dentist/surgeon - stop the drug before planned surgery or dental procedures
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed
Report swelling, decreased urine, or severe fatigue (kidney/liver effects)
pk: Antitumor effect over weeks; BP rise can occur early (within days)
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); keep in original package
pearls: Hypertension is the most common and earliest adverse effect - control BP before starting and monitor closely.
Withhold lenvatinib at least 1 week before elective surgery and resume only after adequate wound healing.
Hypothyroidism/elevated TSH is common, including in patients with thyroid cancer on suppression - monitor and adjust thyroid replacement.
Proteinuria, GI perforation/fistula, and arterial thromboembolism are class antiangiogenic toxicities requiring vigilance.
missed: If a dose is missed and cannot be taken within 12 hours, skip that dose and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take two doses to make up.
overdose: No specific antidote. The most likely adverse effects relate to exaggerated pharmacology (severe hypertension, diarrhea, fatigue, proteinuria). Discontinue, provide supportive care, and manage toxicities (e.g., antihypertensives) as indicated.
